newsitem.title: UK: Cocoa 1996/97 deficit said forecast at 259,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Cocoa 1996/97 deficit said forecast at 259,000 T.

text.p: Trade sources say that a UK-based commodities trading house on Friday have projected a world cocoa deficit of 259,000 tonnes for the 1996/97 (October-September) crop year.
But there was no immediate confirmation of the report, said to be issued for private clients only.

The estimate surpassed a forecast made in September by the International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) which saw the deficit at 225,000 tonnes compared with an estimated surplus of 120,000 tonnes for 1995/96.
The ICCO's deficit estimate was based on an Ivorian production figure this season of 950,000 tonnes, down from around 1.2 million tonnes in 1995/96.
Traders' deficit estimates range between 100,000 and 200,000 tonnes, but earlier this week U.S. brokers Merrill Lynch said the figure was likely to be much smaller at 87,000 tonnes.
Ivory Coast's Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze last month forecast the 1996/97 crop at between 891,000 and 1,009,000 tonnes.
Deficit projections are the main talking point of the market which is already reeling from a record production last year in the world's biggest grower Ivory Coast.
Some analysts say even if there is a deficit, carryover stocks from last season would be enough to ensure sufficient supplies.

The London futures market took the new deficit projection in its stride, with the benchmark March contract standing just one stg down at midday at 1,013 stg a tonne. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 8072
